raw_segments.text: From about the middle of the 14th to the beginning of the 16th century, what was reckoned the
reasonable and moderate—that is, the ordinary or average price of wheat—seems to have
sunk gradually to about one half of this price, so as at last to have fallen to about two
ounces of silver, tower weight, equal to about ten shillings of our present money.
It continued to be estimated at this price till about $15.70.
